candidates.title: Depth Pro 2: Sharp and Temporally Consistent Metric Monocular Depth
candidates.summary: We present Depth Pro 2, an approach to estimating dense metric depth for images and video at full resolution. By analyzing prior methods for monocular depth estimation, we find that they commonly trade off temporal consistency and boundary sharpness: multi-frame methods favor consistency, single-frame methods favor sharpness. To overcome this trade-off, we train a single, scalable network that processes both images and video and predicts depth maps at native resolution. Depth Pro 2 produces depth maps that are metrically accurate, sharp, and temporally consistent all at once, outperforming…

candidates.title: Split-and-Scale Latent 3D Representations
candidates.summary: Latent 3D representations have significantly expanded the capabilities of modern shape modeling, enabling compact encoding of 3D scenes and supporting powerful 3D generative models. Despite this progress, current representations struggle to capture the fine details of complex objects, fundamentally limited by the capacity of their latents. However, scaling latent capacity at training time is computationally expensive and often infeasible under memory limits, and naively increasing the number of latents at inference fails to make effective use of the added capacity. candidates.title: Theoretical Limits of Language Model Alignment
candidates.summary: Language model (LM) alignment improves model outputs to reflect human preferences while preserving the capabilities of the base model. The most common alignment approaches are (i) reinforcement learning, which maximizes the expected reward under a KL-divergence constraint, and (ii) best-of-NNN alignment, which selects the highest-reward output among NNN independent samples. Despite their widespread use, the fundamental limits of reward improvement under a KL budget remain poorly understood. candidates.title: vllm-project/vllm release: v0.34.0
candidates.summary: # v0.34.0 **1,061 commits from 412 contributors (120 new).** Thank you! ## TL;DR - **10 new models** (Mistral Large 4, MiniMax-M3.1-Flash, Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe, and more!) - **Extensible KV cache is on by default:** vLLM sizes the KV cache from memory actually free after warmup, so most models get a bigger cache and more throughput - in most cases you should now **remove `gpu_memory_utilization`** from your configs. - **Model Runner V1 is gone.** Model Runner V2 is now the only GPU runner. - **Big speedups** on Blackwell and MI355X: up to 1.95× decode (Step5 on GB200), 1.6× throughput

candidates.summary: Prompting language models to verbalize stepwise numerical confidence during generation is an increasingly popular approach for triggering backtracking and error correction in agentic reasoning. candidates.title: CTLink: A Text-Prompted Segmentation Model for Linking Radiology Report Findings to 3D Chest CT Scans
candidates.summary: Radiology reports describe findings in text only, without visually marking them on the scan, so readers cannot directly see which abnormality each reported finding refers to. We introduce CTLink, a text-prompted 3D segmentation model that segments findings described in a chest CT report. CTLink was trained on 4123 noncontrast chest CT scans with 9547 segmented report findings, including ReXGroundingCTv2, a newly annotated dataset of 1134 scans and 1895 findings with every instance of each finding segmented. However, the library is laborious to create and maintain, and frozen when new query types, evidence formats, and failure modes are encountered in the wild.
